# Data

Every dataset this study uses, where it comes from, the terms it is under and
how it was checked. Generated data are regenerated from the released code with
the recorded seeds; external data are not redistributed here.

## Generated by the released code

### Application training set (D1)

Produced by the gravothermal solver through `scripts/gen_dataset.py`, with base
seeds 20260827, 30260827 and 40260827: 1300 training, 100 out-of-distribution
parameter and 100 out-of-distribution initial-condition trajectories. Every run
stores its seed, so any trajectory is exactly reproducible; the set takes about
ten minutes on twenty cores. Written to `data/d1/` as HDF5: the density and
velocity fields on a log-radius by normalised-time grid, with each run's
cross-section parameters, initial-condition family and parameter, collapse
time, seed, termination status and wall time, and the base seed, creation time
and solver settings as file attributes.

Coverage: the Yukawa-Born cross-section (70%) with log10 sigma0-hat in
[-1.5, 0.7] and log10 w-hat in [-1, 1.5], and a constant cross-section (30%)
with log10 sigma-hat in [-2, 0.5]; initial conditions NFW (35%), cored NFW
(30%) and generalised NFW (35%). The constant-cross-section subset carries
w-hat = 1 exactly, so in the (log sigma, log w) plane it lies on a line; a
Gaussian-process baseline needs a nugget for that reason.

### Benchmark sets

The four reference systems are generated by `scripts/sc_gen.py --all --n 600`
(about 15 s on 22 cores) and the SIDM set is re-exported from D1 by
`scripts/sc_import_sidm.py`, into `data/sc/`. Per-system requested, kept and
failed counts, the normalised-time grid and generation times are recorded in
`data/sc/manifest.json`, the one file under `data/` the release carries.

### Fischer, Yu & Dolag (2025)

Downloaded from
`https://homepages.usm.uni-muenchen.de/mfischer/data/Fischer2025b/isolated/r80_N5e7_RC15_OA5e-4_GT2.5e-2_SL1.0/`:
`energy.txt` and snapshots 000, 010, 020, 030, 040, 045 and 051, each
1,600,006,576 bytes (identical sizes, so complete), about 11 GB in all. Each
snapshot holds 5x10^7 dark-matter particles in HDF5 `PartType1`, and the run is
non-cosmological. Halo: NFW with r_s = 1.28 kpc, rho_s = 4.42x10^7 Msun/kpc^3
and a constant sigma/m = 80 cm^2/g (dimensionless sigma-hat = 0.9455). Units
are kpc, km/s and 10^10 Msun, with time in kpc/(km/s) = 0.978 Gyr. The
velocity-dependent runs of the same paper are not publicly linked.

### SIDM Concerto

The analysis uses the `LMC_Halo104` subset of the public release, 3.9 GB of
171.6 GB: `LMC_Halo104_GroupSIDM_particles.tar`, `LMC_Halo104_CDM_particles.tar`,
the two `*_RCT.tar` catalogues and `LMC_Halo104_GroupSIDM_parametric.tar`. It is
a dark-matter-only cosmological zoom-in with particle mass 6.3x10^3 Msun and
softening 40 pc/h. Its `GroupSIDM` cross-section,
`dsigma/dcos(theta) = sigma0 w^4 / 2[w^2 + v^2 sin^2(theta/2)]^2` with
sigma0/m = 147.1 cm^2/g and w = 120 km/s, is the Yukawa-Born form the solver
implements, and maps to sigma-hat 0.03-2.04 and w-hat 0.74-6.91, inside the
training range.

Two unit conventions matter. In the public catalogues, `out_sidm.txt` radii
are kpc/h at h = 0.7 while `log.txt` radii are already physical kpc. In the
merger trees, radii are comoving kpc/h and velocities physical km/s. Applying
h twice to either drops the halo matching to zero.

The public release carries z = 0 only. The per-halo merger trees for
`LMC_Halo104`, which the release describes as too large to upload, were
supplied by the suite's authors on request. At their direction they are cited
to the SIDM Concerto paper and its Zenodo release, of which they are intended
to be part. No explicit grant to redistribute was requested or given, so they
are not included here; a reader who needs them should check the Zenodo record
and otherwise ask the Concerto authors for the `Halo104` consistent-trees
output of the `GroupSIDM` and `CDM` runs. The files as received:

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `Halo104_trees/cdm_trees/tree_0_0_0.dat` | 5,354,201,790 | verified by offset closure |
| `Halo104_trees/cdm_trees/locations.dat` | 1,201,900 | `ca0c9d3218ff7f114293c3a8f90c84d9e5583ef9090863ac47e13dbf749a8a0f` |
| `Halo104_trees/cdm_trees/forests.list` | 584,715 | `63081ad4909f1f18ab0591224babd9301347629fbe800bccc7c03c7214fa328b` |
| `Halo104_trees/GroupSIDM_trees/tree_0_0_0.dat` | 4,852,386,504 | verified by offset closure |
| `Halo104_trees/GroupSIDM_trees/locations.dat` | 1,072,511 | `f96ff3f65182d56ee11585159cf29ae45efd24912501cb20d6af6c87eccdcb46` |
| `Halo104_trees/GroupSIDM_trees/forests.list` | 521,769 | `659ac6c54037133bbae117f06eecf83de30b2c6165c2c1f5d169e14489aa2a2c` |

The two tree files are checked by self-consistency rather than a stored
digest: `scripts/fetch_concerto_trees.py --verify-only` requires each to be
longer than the largest byte offset in its own `locations.dat`, the condition a
truncated download fails, and `scripts/concerto_trees.py` reads each tree by
seeking to its offset rather than by a capped stream, which would silently cut
the largest trees short. On receipt, 32,483 CDM and 28,986 GroupSIDM tree roots
joined one to one to their z = 0 catalogues, and the host's main branch ran 236
snapshots from z = 19 to z = 0. Everything derived from the trees, including
the per-halo identities in `results/e32/controls.npz`, is in the archival
record, so the analysis can be re-derived without them; only a re-extraction
needs the trees themselves.

## Considered and not used

| Dataset | Reason |
|---|---|
| DARKSKIES (A&A 703, A112, 2025) | velocity-independent with sigma/m <= 0.2 cm^2/g: clusters that barely form cores and do not collapse |
| BAHAMAS-SIDM | cosmological, constant cross-section, cluster scale |
| Magneticum SIDM | cosmological, constant cross-section |
| IllustrisTNG, FLAMINGO | cold dark matter only |
| `ymzhong/gravothermal` | no licence file, so not redistributable; the GravothermalSIDM implementation is used instead |
